amendment.text: Savannah's Sec. 8-1002 does not touch the toilet-count table, the half-and-half split, rounding or urinals. It restates the single-user rule (403.1.2) and the separate-facilities rule (403.2) with the same small-occupancy exceptions as the state (15 or fewer in total; mercantile 100 or fewer; business 25 or fewer), and adds two exceptions: single-user rooms need not be designated by sex, and a shared room for both sexes may replace separate rooms if each toilet is in a floor-to-ceiling compartment with a lockable door (new 405.3.4.1), urinals are in a visually separated area or in stalls, and the common sink area is not closed off by a door. The amendment is written against the 2018 edition. Georgia's 2026 amendments to the 2024 edition delete Exception 6 to 403.2 (the shared all-gender option) statewide, and state law requires a local amendment to be no less stringent than the state code. Whether Savannah still applies its Exception 6 was not found in anything read.
amendment.quote: Pursuant to §OCGA 8-2-25 the following additions, deletions, or revisions to the International Plumbing Code 2018 edition, as amended by the State of Georgia and this article constitute the minimum Standard Plumbing Code for the City of Savannah, Georgia. Section 403.1.2 of the International Plumbing Code is revised to read as follows: 403.1.2 Single-user toilet and bathing room fixtures. The plumbing fixtures located in single-user toilet and bathing rooms, including family or assisted use toilet and bathing rooms that are required by Section 1109.2.1 of the International Building Code, shall contribute toward the total number of required plumbing fixtures for a building or tenant space. Single-user toilet and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet rooms and bathing rooms shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex. Section 403.2 of the International Plumbing Code is amended by adding exceptions (5) & (6): 403.2 Separate facilities. Where plumbing fixtures are required, separate facilities shall be provided for each sex. Exceptions: Separate facilities shall not be required for dwelling units and sleeping units. Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required to be designated by sex where single-user toilet rooms are provided in accordance with Section 403.1.2. Separate facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by both sexes and privacy for water closets is provided in accordance with Section 405.3.4. Urinals shall be located in an area visually separated from the remainder of the facility or each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall. Section 405.3.4.1 is added to the 2018 International Plumbing Code: 405.3.4.1 Privacy for Non-Separated Facilities. Where shared facilities are provided per Section 403.2 (6), each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls that extend from the floor to the ceiling and a lockable door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy. The common lavatory area shall not be closed off by a door to the remainder of the building. (Ord. of 1-19-2017(5); Ord. of 7-20-2017(1); Ord. of 7-18-2019(31), § 1, Ord. of 12-5-2019(48), § 2, Ord. of 02-25-2021(36), § 1, Ord. of 5-12-2022(14), § 1, Ord. of 7-14-2022(15), § 1) Effective on: 7/14/2022
amendment.stringency_quote: The requirements in the proposed local amendment cannot be less stringent than the requirements in the state minimum standard code.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Savannah job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material for coastal humidity and see the rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Savannah hotels, restaurants, schools and port warehouses, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Georgia's plumbing rules set the number of toilets by how many people use the building, and Savannah enforces them without changing the counts. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Savannah requires a permit to build, alter or repair a building, and lets ordinary minor repairs go ahead without one. The city code doesn't say which work counts as a minor repair and doesn't name toilet partitions, so ask Savannah Development Services whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a one-person restroom must be marked as open to everyone. Georgia's rules call for separate men's and women's rooms for the toilets a building must have, and in 2026 the state removed the option that lets a shared all-gender room take their place. Savannah's city code still carries its own version of that option, written for an earlier edition of the plumbing rules: a shared room where every toilet sits in a compartment with floor-to-ceiling walls and a lockable door, urinals are in stalls or screened from view, and the sink area is not closed off by a door. Ask Savannah Development Services which rule applies before planning one. State law requires public schools, and private schools that compete against them, to provide separate shared restrooms for each sex.
page.stalls_after: These are state minimums for the whole building, and Savannah's city code does not change them. An office that holds 25 people or fewer, or any space that holds 15 or fewer, may use one restroom for everyone.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or Savannah Development Services sets the final number.
page.install_rule: A contractor who does work that needs a Savannah permit must follow the state and local licensing rules, and where Georgia requires a license, gives the city the license number before the permit is issued. Georgia licenses general contractors, and limited specialty trade work may be exempt, so confirm with the Georgia State Licensing Board for Residential and General Contractors whether your installer needs a state license. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: Where Georgia requires a contractor license, the contractor gives Savannah the license number before a permit is issued.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Georgia has no state wage law for public construction, so a set wage applies only on federally funded projects, under federal law. For a carpenter on building work in Chatham County that rate is $19.13 an hour plus $0.30 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7% in Savannah: 4% state, 1% local option, 1% schools and 1% special purpose tax, all three collected across Chatham County.
page.buyers_extra: - **Hotels and visitor attractions:** finishes that match the property in guest-facing restrooms, HDPE or phenolic where crowds and frequent cleaning are hard on stalls.
